wholeMethodJudgment.reason: The primary random sampling unit is now a spatially distinct identified plant with a unique plant ID. Exactly one comparably mature/positioned leaf is linked to each sampled plant; missing or damaged leaves and actual plant numbers are recorded. Additional leaves are explicitly nested repeated measurements, not independent plants. A predefined documented random plant-selection rule prevents outcome-driven substitution. Spatial distinction does not imply genetic independence because clonal growth remains possible. Two observed sites describe these samples and are not replicated site-effect experiments. Leaf measurements across sampled plants permit bounded leaf-trait variation descriptions but cannot prove inheritance, adaptation, selection or allele frequencies. This directly resolves the previous leaves-as-plant-replicates defect.
